abstract: The new energy demonstration city policy is an initiative in China aimed at fostering an environmentally friendly society. This study constructs a quasi-natural experiment with this policy and adopts a difference-in-differences model based on the data of Chinese A-share listed companies to investigate the impact of the new energy demonstration city policy on corporate ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) performance. The results show that the policy significantly improves firms’ ESG performance, and this finding remains robust across a series of robustness tests. The heterogeneity analysis suggests that the policy’s drivers have differential impacts on different types of firms, and the most pronounced positive effects are observed in technology-intensive and non-state-owned firms. Finally, this study reveals that green innovation, reputational risk, and financing constraints are potential mechanisms of action of the policy in influencing firms’ ESG performance. Unlike previous studies that typically examine these factors in isolation, our integrated framework reveals the interconnected pathways through which energy transition policies drive corporate sustainability outcomes. This research provides valuable insights into the impact of the energy transition on corporate ESG performance, highlighting the positive effects of new energy macro policies on the sustainable development of enterprises.

abstract: Aligned with China’s low-carbon transformation goals, this study assesses the impact of two key policies on household adoption of new energy vehicles (NEVs): the administrative Fuel Vehicle Purchase Restriction (FVPR) policy and the fiscal incentive New Energy Demonstration City (NEDC) program. Using 2019 China Household Finance Survey (CHFS) data and the Heckman model to address sample selection bias, results show both policies significantly stimulate NEV adoption, with the FVPR policy exerting a more substantial influence. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the FVPR policy drives NEV uptake across all households. In contrast, the NEDC policy is effective for urban households but not for rural households, and for low-income households but not for high-income households. These findings provide actionable insights for policymakers globally: combining regulatory constraints with targeted fiscal incentives can optimize the promotion of NEVs. Future research could utilize panel data to examine the long-term effects of policy adjustments and advances in battery technology, or conduct in-depth analyses of rural adoption barriers through charging infrastructure cost-benefit studies.

abstract: This paper examines how better coordination could improve a financial institution’s overall efficiency. A two-stage data envelopment analysis is proposed in which the overall efficiency of a decision-making unit is a function of the stage-wise efficiencies, along with coordination efficiency, which is the efficiency gains from optimal coordination among the production stages beyond those captured at the individual stages. Microfinance institutions use shareholders’ equity, borrowing from institutional sources, and expenses as inputs to generate deposits and gross loans, which are then utilized to produce revenue and outreach. Using a worldwide dataset of 679 microfinance institutions, this paper found that the explanatory power of overall efficiency improves substantially when the coordination efficiency measure, along with the efficiency of separate stages, is considered in the regression framework. Our findings are robust across varying ownership structures of MFIs. The proposed model is likely to help the managers understand the origins of inefficiencies, whether they are ascribed to each stage or to their synchronization.
title: Does better coordination improve overall efficiency? Evidence from microfinance institutions

abstract: This study investigates the impact of the VAT credit refund reform on the cash dividend policies of listed companies. The results indicate that the VAT credit refund reform significantly reduces both the willingness to distribute and the actual levels of cash dividends, with these conclusions remaining robust after a series of robustness tests. Mechanism analyses reveal that VAT credit refunds enhance the liquidity of treated firms, thereby stimulating their investment propensity while reducing their refinancing needs, which ultimately leads to a decline in cash dividend payouts. Our heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect of the credit refund policy on cash dividend distributions varies across firms at different stages of their life cycle, with a more pronounced impact on growth-stage firms compared to those in maturity or decline stages. Further research suggests that, under the influence of the VAT credit refund policy, reductions in cash dividends positively affect firm value. This study not only expands the literature on the economic consequences of tax neutrality reforms but also offers valuable insights for policymakers seeking to understand the micro-level effects of tax reforms on firm behaviour, while contributing empirical evidence on the factors influencing cash dividends from the perspective of indirect taxation.

abstract: Governments worldwide have adopted varying policies towards cryptocurrency. In this study, we examine the connectedness between cryptocurrency prices and segmented technology sectors in China, the United States, and global markets with 13,225 observations made 26 January 2021–11 December 2023. Given differing regulatory policies, we find the effects of cryptocurrency on technology sectors do not exhibit a significant heterogeneity in terms of returns or volatility spillovers. Cryptocurrency dominates the network with technological innovation at country and global level markets. The results demonstrate that government-imposed cryptocurrency banning policies are limited in suppressing the impact of cryptocurrency. Using a machine learning GA2M algorithm, we find that the U.S. consumer digital services sector has the strongest impact on cryptocurrency returns, whereas software technology demonstrates a stronger interaction with cryptocurrencies than does the hardware sector. This suggests that investors and policymakers, regardless of regulatory stance, should closely monitor cryptocurrency price movements for informed decision-making in complex ecosystem environments.

abstract: We use the shift to working from home (WFH) induced by the COVID-19 lockdown to examine the determinants of WFH productivity among workers in Saudi Arabia, a country that imposed one of the world’s most stringent pandemic lockdowns while undergoing rapid female labour-market liberalization. We find that the ease of performing job tasks from home is the strongest predictor of maintaining or improving productivity. Collaboration and communication also matter: frequent meetings and relationships with colleagues and clients unaffected by WFH are associated with higher productivity. Having a dedicated workspace and feeling supported by one’s organization further enhance outcomes, particularly in larger firms. Finally, productivity declines more sharply with the number of children for women than for men, highlighting the continued influence of family responsibilities on remote work outcomes. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the conditions under which WFH can be productive in emerging economies experiencing major institutional and social transitions.
title: Productivity when working from home: evidence from Saudi Arabia

abstract: This study employs 56 macroeconomic indicators to forecast the annual carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in Korea. The 56 macroeconomic indicators are analogous to those utilized in FRED-MD and represent Korean data from 1985 to 2022. This study uses various machine learning techniques, including XGBoost, complete subset regression, and random forest models. The Boruta algorithm, a variable selection technique based on the random forest model, is applied to identify the variables that exert the greatest influence on annual CO2 emissions forecasting. Furthermore, out-of-sample multi-period forecasts are evaluated for each forecasting model to select that which best predicts annual CO2 emissions. The results demonstrate that the random forest model and the random forest model with the Boruta algorithm exhibit the most favourable out-of-sample performance in short-term forecasting. In selecting variables to predict CO2 emissions using the Boruta algorithm, the production index and shipment index of producers in the electricity, gas, steam, and air conditioning supply industry are identified as significant for enhancing the predictive capacity of the model. The findings provide key policy insights for carbon emissions management. Leveraging real-time macroeconomic indicators can help policymakers address delays in CO 2 emissions data, enabling adaptive regulations that balance economic growth and environmental sustainability.
title: Forecasting carbon dioxide emissions using macroeconomic indicators: a machine learning approach

abstract: Interval-valued time series (ITS), frequently encountered in financial applications, often arise from cross-sectional aggregation (e.g. daily highest and lowest returns across a portfolio) or temporal aggregation (e.g. intraday highs and lows). Despite the extreme-value nature of ITS components, existing models seldom exploit extreme value theory (EVT). This article introduces a new EVT-based framework for modelling ITS using the Fréchet distribution, a heavy-tailed case of the generalized extreme value (GEV) family well suited to financial extremes. Extending the autoregressive conditional Fréchet (AcF) model of Zhao et al. (2018), we propose a novel specification in which the range, the difference between the upper and lower bounds, drives the scale and tail parameters of the Fréchet distribution. This structure incorporates information from both bounds, improves numerical stability, and captures the empirical link between volatility clustering and the clustering of extreme events. The model is estimated via maximum likelihood, and simulations confirm strong finite-sample performance. Empirical studies using daily returns of DJI30 constituents and 5-minute S&P 500 returns show that the proposed model achieves superior in-sample fit and out-of-sample predictive accuracy compared with competing approaches. We also identify significant tail connectedness between interval bounds. A trading application demonstrates model’s practical value.
title: Modelling interval-valued time series, an extreme value theory approach

abstract: This study develops a comprehensive machine learning (ML)-based model to identify the key determinants of total factor productivity (TFP) in 29 manufacturing industries listed in China over the period 2015–2022, with a particular focus on technological innovation, corporate operation, and executive characteristics. Among various ML models tested, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) demonstrates the highest predictive accuracy. Using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), we find that R&D investment and inventory turnover are the two strongest positive predictors of TFP, highlighting the importance of technological innovation and operation efficiency. Moreover, the analysis reveals significant heterogeneity across corporate contexts, with customer concentration exerting a stronger negative effect on TFP in non-high-tech industries and asset-heavy enterprises. These findings highlight the relative importance of micro-level drivers of productivity to enhance industrial competitiveness.

abstract: Providing inclusive environments has become a primary tenet of modern societies and organizations. The use of gender-inclusive language (GIL) is often considered an instrument that can promote inclusion, yet little is known about its effects on relevant economic behaviors and on gender gaps in the labor market. GIL avoids the masculine “default” (common to many languages) by either explicitly mentioning both masculine and feminine (pro)nouns, or replacing them with nongendered (pro)nouns. Here we study the causal short-run impact of GIL on competitiveness and leadership in the laboratory, with two different language samples—English and German—which differ, among other things, in the extent to which gender is embedded linguistically. We vary GIL in experimental instructions across three treatments ([Formula: see text]): a masculine baseline condition, a condition with feminine and masculine (pro)nouns, and a condition with nongendered (pro)nouns. We find that participants who identify as female and participants who identify as male compete, stand for leadership, and vote on leader candidates similarly across all treatments, in either language. Furthermore, we find no treatment differences in participants’ feelings of inclusion and perceived entitlement. In sum, there is a lack of support for GIL having short-term causal effects on competitive and leadership behavior and inclusion perceptions. This paper was accepted by Marie-Claire Villeval, behavioral economics and decision analysis. abstract_zh: 提供包容性环境已成为现代社会和组织的一项首要原则。使用性别包容性语言（GIL）常被视为一种能够促进包容的工具，但人们对其对相关经济行为以及劳动力市场中性别差距的影响知之甚少。GIL通过明确提及男性和女性（代）名词，或用无性别（代）名词替代它们，避免了男性“默认”（许多语言中常见）。在此，我们在实验室中研究GIL对竞争力和领导力的因果短期影响，采用两个不同的语言样本——英语和德语——它们在诸多方面有所不同，其中包括性别在语言中嵌入的程度。我们在实验指令中变化GIL，分为三种处理（[公式：见正文]）：男性基线条件、包含女性和男性（代）名词的条件，以及包含无性别（代）名词的条件。我们发现，自我认同为女性和自我认同为男性的参与者，在两种语言的所有处理中，其竞争、竞选领导职位以及对领导候选人投票的行为都相似。此外，我们发现参与者的包容感和感知权利在处理之间没有差异。总之，缺乏支持GIL对竞争和领导行为以及包容感知具有短期因果效应的证据。本文由Marie-Claire Villeval，行为经济学与决策分析领域接受。资助：本工作得到奥地利科学基金[资助号SFB F63]、英国研究与创新[资助号MR/T020253/1]、埃克塞特大学以及雷根斯堡大学基金会Lucia and Dr. Otfried Eberz的支持。补充材料：在线附录和数据文件可在https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04342获取。

abstract: This work explores the preferences that laypeople exhibit when making and evaluating predictions in the form of point estimates (e.g., the high temperature will be 66°). I propose that people typically have diminishing sensitivity to prediction error: the absolute difference between a prediction and a realized outcome. As a result, people often prioritize “being right,“ focusing on achieving near perfect predictions and placing less emphasis on the magnitude of errors when errors occur. Across 16 studies using varying methods and stimuli, participants exhibited multiple behaviors consistent with diminishing sensitivity to prediction error: (i) predicting the mode of distributions, (ii) restricting predictions to possible outcomes, (iii) reporting decreasing reactions to increasing marginal units of error, and (iv) preferring predictive models built with diminishing sensitivity to error. This behavior diverges from traditional methods of building predictive models and common interpretations of people’s predictions, which often prioritize avoiding large errors and assume that people are predicting the mean. Ultimately, this work not only highlights the discrepancies between our current practices and people’s preferences for predictions but also calls for a more thorough exploration of human objectives before we build models for them to use or make inferences about their beliefs in light of a decision they made. This paper was accepted by Jack Soll, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: I thank the University of Chicago Booth School of Business for financial support. Supplemental Material: Preregistrations, materials, data, code, and supplements are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07257 and at ResearchBox at https://researchbox.org/3130 .
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了普通人在以点估计形式（例如，最高气温将为66°）进行预测和评估预测时所表现出的偏好。我提出，人们通常对预测误差——即预测值与实际结果之间的绝对差——具有递减敏感性。因此，人们往往优先考虑“预测准确”，专注于实现接近完美的预测，而在出现误差时较少强调误差的幅度。在16项采用不同方法和刺激材料的研究中，参与者表现出多种与对预测误差的递减敏感性相一致的行为：(i) 预测分布的众数，(ii) 将预测限制在可能结果范围内，(iii) 报告对递增的边际误差单位反应递减，以及 (iv) 偏好以对误差的递减敏感性构建的预测模型。这种行为偏离了构建预测模型的传统方法以及对人们预测的常见解读，后者往往优先考虑避免大误差，并假设人们在预测均值。最终，本研究不仅凸显了我们当前实践与人们对预测的偏好之间的差异，也呼吁在构建供人们使用的模型、或根据人们所做决策推断其信念之前，对人类目标进行更彻底的探索。本文由Jack Soll、行为经济学与决策分析领域接收。资助：我感谢芝加哥大学布斯商学院提供的财务支持。补充材料：预注册、材料、数据、代码和补充内容可在 https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07257 以及 ResearchBox 的 https://researchbox.org/3130 获取。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Understanding People’s Preferences for Predictions: People Prioritize Being Right over Minimizing How Wrong They Are in Expectation
title_zh: 理解人们对预测的偏好：人们更重视正确性而非最小化预期错误程度
